NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a special meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be held on
Thursday, March 26, 2026, commencing at 9:00 a.m., in Ruth Reese Hall of the Alhambra
Civic Center Library, 101 South First Street, Alhambra, California, pursuant to the order of

and Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

An agenda of such special meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and
made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

Addressing the Council:

addressing the Council. Any person wishing to address the Council during the meeting should
complete a Speaker Request Card and submit it to the City Clerk so the City Council knows you
wish to speak. When called upon by the presiding officer, please step to the microphone.

telephone. Staff will unmute speakers participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your
name when it is your time to speak. When calling in using a telephone press *9 to raise your
hand and press *6 to unmute yourself when called.

The maximum time for addressing the Council is 5 minutes for each agendized item.

 CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M26-33

The City Clerk hereby reports that she duly gave notice of the Special Meeting of the City
Council being held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

1.  CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION – F2M26-27

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William Kelly,
  President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group, held a strategic planning
  session on March 3, 2026 to review and update the City’s Strategic Plan adopted in
  2025. The Draft Strategic Plan contains six Goals, defined as follows: Goal 1: Enhance
  Public Safety; Goal 2: Improve Infrastructure and Mobility; Goal 3: Create a Strong
  Financial Base and Strong Economic Base (Economic Development); Goal 4: Enhance
  Transparency and Open Governance; Goal 5: Promote Sustainability; and, Goal 6:
  Improve Housing Opportunities, and an Implementation Plan to provide details and
  metrics to monitor the Plan. The City Council will review, clarify and discuss the updates
  to finalize the 2026 Strategic Plan.

ADJOURNMENT: If three (3) or more Council Members choose not to participate in Item No.
2 (Media Communications Training), the meeting will be adjourned. If a quorum of the Council
elects to participate in Item No. 2, the meeting will continue.

2.  MEDIA COMMUNICATIONS TRAINING – F2M26-16

  Mr. Paul Omodt of Omodt and Associates will present information and provide training
  for City Council Members on the topic of navigating media communications.

ADJOURNMENT: The next regularly scheduled meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be
held on Monday, April 13, 2026, in the Alhambra City Hall Council Chambers, 111 South First
Street, Alhambra, California, commencing at 6:00 p.m.

  NOTICE
Agenda Items: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to the items listed
on this agenda are on file with the City Clerk in Alhambra City Hall, located at 111 South First Street,
Alhambra, California, and are available for inspection during regular office hours, Monday through
Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. If you would like to sign-up to receive the City Council meeting
agenda and staff reports packet, please visit the City’s website at www.alhambraca.gov and you will
be able to submit your email address on the homepage to the subscription service. Pursuant to
Government Code Section 54957.5(b), materials related to agenda items for regular meetings of the
Alhambra City Council that are distributed less than 72 hours prior to that meeting, will be made
available for public inspection at the Alhambra City Clerk’s Office.

Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City
meeting (including assisted listening devices), please contact the City Clerk's Office at (626) 570-

 MAKING THE MEDIA
WORK FOR YOU
CITY COUNCIL WORK SESSION  FEBRUARY 26, 2025
MARCH 26, 2026
 ABOUT PAUL OMODT

Omodt & Associates Critical Communication
Founder and Principal

35+ Years Public Relations Experience
Professional Spokesperson
Former City of St. Louis Park City Council Member
League of Minnesota Cities Conference Presenter
CJPIA Conference Presenter
Adjunct Professor, University of St. Thomas
Professional Designations Include: ABC, APR, Fellow
PRSA, MBA, SCMP
 TODAY’S BIG QUESTION:

 What if there was an organization NOBODY liked, trusted or respected – and yet they
  were vital to your long-term success.

  Would you trust this organization
  to accurately tell the world about you?
 WHY WORK WITH THE MEDIA?

Public perception of local Alhambra issues is shaped by (in this order):

  • Preconception, what we believe or know, up until that point in time
  (including your city’s brand!)
  • Word of mouth by trusted source
  • Traditional local media sources (third party validation)
  • Social media
 WHY WORK WITH THE MEDIA?

• Media coverage is credible, cost-effective
  and timely means of communicating with
  your audiences

• Media exposure heightens your image as
  a knowledge expert

• Media coverage is an excellent means of
  recognition for what you do and what the
  city does – it re-enforces positives and
  brand positions
 WHY WORK WITH THE MEDIA?

• The media will cover your story whether or not you agree to do an
  interview

• This is your chance to shape, refine and control the message

• Because there are “Five C’s” of effective media relations…and if you
  use them correctly, the media can and will work for you…the Five C’s
  are…
 CONTROL STARTS NOW!

• Start considering your work with the local media as performances – not
  interviews

• In performances, you lead

• In interviews, the reporter leads

• It is best for YOU to be in the lead and for you to exercise control
 CONTROL THE OPPORTUNITY!

Ask questions! The first questions always come from YOU! Ask questions
such as these:
  What is the focus of the article or report
  What information do you need?
  What is your deadline?
  Have you interviewed anybody else?

But before you start, don’t answer any questions yet:
  Remember, you are always on the record
  Be sure you know the reporter, the publication –
  never -- ever -- talk to strangers!
 CONTROL STARTS WITH YOUR TEAM!
Consider reporters an extension of your team.

Understanding: You want something, they want something. You have
something to give, they have something to give.

What reporters want from YOU and YOU want from reporters:
  Responsiveness
  Respect
  Honesty
  Clear, concise, and quick information
  Help tell a story
 THE ZEN OF THE PERFORMANCE
Remember: You are always on stage!

Be your best, authentic self

Use your face and voice to manifest your
message

Affirm your authority and enjoy the
opportunity

Be calm, relaxed – and remember the
two-way relationship involves your
ability to share information!
 BEFORE YOUR PERFORMANCE, GET READY!

Always: prepare three to five key messages that speak directly to your
audience

Practice out loud

Don’t memorize – internalize

Use tools available: Pitch Plan, Website, Fact Sheets, Talking points

Live the Alhambra brand!
 BODY LANGUAGE IS LANGUAGE

Some body language basics:

Do’s  Don’t’s

  Use affirmative body language  Slouch
  Make eye contact  Fidget
  Use your hands  Fold your arms
  Exude confidence  Give off a negative vibe
 WHAT’S RECALLED?
TONE, CONFIDENCE, AUTHENTICITY

Proactively set who you are! You need to determine what part of yourself
you project

Tone – use your voice to convey meaning

Tone – should match the content

Play your voice – use the variety in your voice
 THREE DO’S

Be “on” from the moment you walk into the room or are with reporters (at
an event, on a tour, etc.) – your performance begins before you see or talk
to the reporter

Use positive language and phrases – be for something!

Speak of challenges and situations – not problems
 THREE DON’TS

Don’t rush – take your time

Don’t speculate, exaggerate or make anything up – if you don’t know say
you don’t know (but you will try to get the answer)

Don’t ever, ever lie
 DURING YOUR PERFORMANCE

Assume EVERYTHING is on the record

Beginnings, Middles, Ends
  In the beginning, you make an opening statement
  In the middle, you ensure your key points are made
  In the end, you make a closing argument

Use active listening skills – Don’t be afraid to ask for refinements to
questions

Answering a question is a three part process:
  Listen -- Think -- Respond
 BUILD BRIDGES!
Use bridging: transitioning from a difficult subject to one of your key
messages
  “Yes…” (the answer) “and in addition to that” (the bridge)
  “No…” (the answer) “let me explain…”
  “I don’t know…but what I do know is…”
  “That’s the way it used to be…here’s what we do now…”
 WAVE YOUR FLAG!

Use ‘flagging’: verbally highlighting your key messages to make them
stand out
  ‘The most important thing to remember is’
  ‘I think it all boils down to these three things’
 HOOKS, COMMENTS, UNDERSTANDING

Suggest the next question or set a hook – you should ask me…

Avoid ‘no comment’: “I can’t answer that question, but what I can tell you is
this…”

• More specifically, for pending legal matters: "We can't comment on
  pending legal matters. What we can say is..."
• For non-pending legal matters: “While we can't discuss [X], I can say
  [what is appropriate].”

Stand your ground – “I understand your question, but it touches on
confidential information, so we’ll just have to leave it at that.”
 PREPARATION IS KEY

Even in friendly, two-way street exchanges, there can be difficult
questions – don’t be offended – be prepared and walk toward the question

Prepare in advance – make sure you can answer the difficult question

Part of most crisis response situations involve the media – so, being
prepared with trained spokespeople and approved key messages are key
 CITIES CAN BE A MYSTERY TO MANY

The reporter may/may not know acronyms, jargon & tech speak, but
remember, the ultimate audience is the reader/viewer/listener/grower

Acronyms can be dangerous

Assuming shared knowledge can be dangerous
 EXAMPLES, METAPHORS, STORIES

It’s alright to use analogies and metaphors to make and reinforce your
point

It’s alright to speak plainly in language, metaphor and analogies reporters
will understand

Good stories are always remembered most
  KEY MESSAGES

Key messages are your safe harbor

MINUTES
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Special Meeting
  March 26, 2026
  9:00 a.m.

ROLL CALL: At 9:15 a.m., on Thursday, March 26, 2026, the Alhambra City Council met in Ruth
Reese Hall of the Alhambra Civic Center Library, 101 South First Street, Alhambra, California.

CITY COUNCIL:  PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
  ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, City Attorney Montes,
Assistant City Clerk Lamb McCarthy, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of Library
Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Human
Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Chief of Police Kennedy,
Deputy Director of Public Works/Utilities Ahlen, Management Analyst Alvarez, Grants Specialist
Taber, Management Analyst – Sustainability Martel, Economic Development Specialist MacCarley

Also present was Facilitator William R. Kelly, President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M26-33

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the Special Meeting of the City Council
being held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

1.  CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION – F2M26-27

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William Kelly,
  President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group, held a strategic planning session on
  March 3, 2026 to review and update the City’s Strategic Plan adopted in 2025. The Draft
  Strategic Plan contained six Goals, defined as follows: Goal 1: Enhance Public Safety; Goal
  2: Improve Infrastructure and Mobility; Goal 3: Create a Strong Financial Base and Strong
  Economic Base (Economic Development); Goal 4: Enhance Transparency and Open
  Governance; Goal 5: Promote Sustainability; and, Goal 6: Improve Housing Opportunities, and
  an Implementation Plan to provide details and metrics to monitor the Plan.

  Public Comment:

  1) Mara KELEDEI, 355 S. Arroyo Dr., San Gabriel, spoke against the installation of security
  cameras in Almansor park. She also suggested devoting more funding towards public
  transportation.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed various items including the 710 freeway
  stub, building heights, the project at 110 S. Chapel Ave., and housing issues.

  3) Nicole JOHNSON spoke against the installation of security cameras in Almansor Park. She
  stated that this was a safe city and discussed surveillance and privacy issues.
  4) Jeremiah spoke against the installation of security cameras in Almansor Park. He further
  discussed surveillance issues and the construction of data centers. He supported Council’s
  recently adopted Resolution regarding Federal Immigration Enforcement in the City.

  1
3-26-26
   5) Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., discussed crime in Almansor Park and spoke against the
  installation of cameras in the park. She went on to discuss issues of trash collection and the
  organic waste program. She spoke about the need for further public education and suggested
  programs in schools.

  6) Monique RANDLE, of SGV Village, spoke against the installation of cameras in Almansor Park
  and discussed issues of surveillance and privacy. She suggesting using City funds to hire more
  staff to patrol the parks.

  7) Siobhan D., via Zoom, spoke against the installation of cameras in Almansor Park and
  discussed issues of surveillance and privacy.

  The City Council reviewed, clarified, and discussed the updates to finalize the 2026 Strategic
  Plan. Council first discussed objectives listed under Goal 1: Enhance Public Safety. Council
  discussed Objective 1.5 pertaining to the installation of cameras in Almansor Park.
  Councilmember LEE suggested combining the Objective with Objective 1.6 for staff to
  research areas that had higher crime rates, suggested private citizens continue to install their
  own cameras, and suggested the City find other ways of deterring crime. Council discussed
  crime in Alhambra and the parks specifically with City Manager BINNQUIST. Councilmember
  WANG, Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER, Councilmember MAZA, and Mayor MALONEY did
  not support the installation of cameras in the parks. Council continued to discuss crime in and
  around the parks. Mr. MAZA suggested removing the Objective from the Strategic Plan. Mr.
  MALONEY supported the suggestion and discussed Objective 1.6 pertaining to Infrastructure
  Improvements as Crime Deterrents. He suggested expanding the scope.

  Council discussed Objective 1.1 pertaining to Public Education programs and staff provided
  attendance information as requested by Council. Ms. WANG and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed
  the Neighborhood Watch meetings and Community Academy meetings. Council continued to
  discuss the various programs and meetings. Ms. BINNQUIST and Police Chief KENNEDY
  provided clarification.

  Ms. WANG discussed Objective 1.6 to Research Infrastructure Improvements to deter crime
  and made suggestions for areas of research such as walkability in downtown area and
  changes to speed limits close to the freeway. Ms. WANG and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed
  funding for Objective 1.2 pertaining to the Street Light Master Plan. Mr. MAZA and Mr.
  MALONEY also discussed Objective 1.2.

  Council discussed Objective 1.3 pertaining to Immigration Concerns and Ms. BINNQUIST
  provided an update. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. MALONEY discussed the potential
  role of the Human Relations Commission and the Council Sub-Committee to continue
  monitoring immigration issues.

  Council discussed Objective 1.4 pertaining to communication with Southern California Edison
  (SCE). Council discussed SCE planned and unplanned outages, notification and
  communication to residents, a presentation from SCE’s representative to the City, concerns
  regarding fire risks, and the City’s relationship with Clean Power Alliance (CPA).

  Ms. BINNQUIST provided an update regarding Objective 2.1 and the 710 project. She stated
  that a meeting with CalTrans was scheduled. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER spoke in support of
  Objective 2.2. Mayor MALONEY, Ms. WANG, and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed Objective 2.3
  related to expanding greenspace through the City. Mr. MALONEY nominated Ms. WANG to
  lead a subcommittee to explore more options for greenspace and Ms. WANG accepted. Ms.
  BINNQUIST stated that Objectives 2.3 and 2.9 would be joined on the Strategic Plan. Mr.
  MALONEY and Mr. MAZA discussed Objective 2.5 pertaining to Open Streets events and Ms.

  2
3-26-26
   BINNQUIST provided clarifications and updates. Ms. WANG and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed
  updates to Objective 2.7 related to the Traffic Calming Policy. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and
  Ms. BINNQUIST discussed updates to Objective 2.8 pertaining to the improvement of City
  Bridges and Objective 2.10 pertaining to the Development of City Branding. Mr. MALONEY
  and Ms. WANG also discussed 2.10. Ms. BINNQUIST provided updates on Objective 2.11
  pertaining to the Seismic Vulnerability Assessment of City Facilities.

  Council discussed Goal 3: Create a Strong Financial Base and Strong Economic Base. Council
  discussed Objective 3.3 pertaining to the exploration of the Downtown Alhambra Business
  Association boundaries. After a discussion between Ms. Wang and Ms. Binnquist, Mr.
  MALONEY suggested a Council sub-committee to explore the development of certain sections
  of Valley Blvd. Ms. WANG and Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER agreed to be a part of the sub-
  committee. Staff agreed to bring back a discussion item to Council regarding economic
  development of Valley Blvd.

  Council determined that Objectives 3.4 and 3.5 would be combined to Strategize the City’s
  pension liability and to Increase City reserves to 30%. The remaining objectives under Goal 3
  would be renumbered accordingly. Council also agreed that staff would review the reserve
  policies of other cities.

  Mr. MALONEY discussed Objective 3.7 pertaining to 2028 Olympic opportunities and reported
  on recent meeting with other mayors. Ms. LEE also discussed the Objective. This objective
  was also changed to “funded” after clarification from staff.

  Council discussed Objective 3.8 pertaining to the Industrial Zone. Council discussed
  suggestions to change the industrial zones to be more walkable, outreach to other businesses,
  and existing businesses in the industrial zone. Ms. BINNQUIST and John BWARIE,
  representing the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce provided clarification regarding the existing
  industrial businesses. Council continued to discuss the industrial zones and Director of
  Community Development HO provided clarification regarding the use of the industrial zone,
  the condition of the current buildings, the types of businesses interested in industrial zones
  such as biomedical technology, and how other neighboring cities have done with their
  industrial zones. Staff agreed to continue to research and report to Council. Ms. WANG and
  Ms. LEE discussed the decline in Alhambra Unified School District enrollment and changes to
  the industrial zone which could help attract families such as housing or family activities.

  Council discussed Objective 3.8 with Ms. BINNQUIST who provided clarification about
  creating a staff position to provide concierge services to new businesses. Ms. WANG
  requested clarification regarding the impact of creating a new position and the possible
  services offered to businesses. Ms. BINNQUIST stated that staff would review and report back
  to Council.

  Council discussed objectives under Goal 4: Enhance Transparency and Open Governance.
  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. MALONEY praised the “GoAlhambra” app. Ms.
  BINNQUIST reported that staff contacted Eagle Scout candidates who would help install
  exterior bulletin boards at Almansor and Granada Park to satisfy Objective 4.4. Council agreed
  to remove the objective as it was complete. Council also agreed to remove Objective 4.5 as
  complete and funded. Council discussed Objective 4.6 pertaining to Technological Upgrades
  at Joslyn Center. Ms. BINNQUIST and Director of Parks and Recreation MACIAS provided
  clarification regarding the current technology at the Joslyn Center as well as budget
  requirements to obtain upgrades.

  Ms. BINNQUIST and Mr. MALONEY discussed Objective 4.7 and stated that Council has not

  3
3-26-26
   yet provided reports regarding their involvement on other meetings attended.

  Council next discussed objectives under Goal 5: Promote Sustainability. Ms. BINNQUIST
  provided an update regarding Objective 5.1 regarding the Sustainability Plan and Mr.
  MALONEY discussed it with her. Mr. MALONEY suggested changing the Strategic Plan
  Objective to “Develop Plan to Incorporate Elements into other Goals.” Council agreed that they
  would continue to review the plan, implement it, and utilize the goals in other aspects. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed Objective 5.3 pertaining to Gateway
  Plaza. Ms. BINNQUIST also reported that staff would bring back a report pertaining to
  Objective 5.4 to Revisit the Tree Ordinance.

  Council discussed Goal 6: Improve Housing Opportunities. Council briefly discussed Objective
  6.3 and the Cesar Chavez Foundation. Ms. BINNQUIST reported that there would be an
  agendized staff report and discussion at the April 13, 2026 City Council meeting for Objective
  6.5 related to Tenant Relocation Assistance. Ms. BINNQUIST also provided an update
  regarding Objective 6.6 regarding the consultant for the next Housing Element preparation.

  Council discussed Objective 6.7 to Review Zoning at Main and Chapel as a case study for a
  possible transition zone. Council discussed the zoning of the area, the existing buildings in the
  area, and how the transition zone would relate to the East Main Corridor. Ms. BINNQUIST and
  Mr. HO provided clarification. Ms. LEE expressed concerns with the Objective and Mr.
  MALONEY, Ms. WANG, and Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER supported further review and
  discussion.

  Council discussed Objective 6.8 to Purchase Apartment Buildings for low-income housing. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER suggested looking at hotels and motels for purchase as well and also
  suggested the City speak to the San Gabriel Valley Housing Trust. Ms. WANG discussed the
  RHNA allocation for Alhambra.

Recess & Reconvene:  Mayor Maloney called for a brief recess at 12:25 p.m. and resumed the
meeting at 12:38 p.m. with all members present.

2.  MEDIA COMMUNICATIONS TRAINING – F2M26-16

  Mr. Paul Omodt of Omodt and Associates presented information and provide training for City
  Council Members on the topic of navigating media communications. The presentation is on file
  in the City Clerk’s office. Council made comments and Mr. OMODT provided clarification. Ms.
  WANG and Mr. OMODT discussed how to address media coverage of an incident that could
  be incorrect or misrepresents the incident.

ADJOURNMENT:  At 1:18 p.m., Mayor Maloney adjourned the meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
  by
  BRIANNA LAMB MCCARTHY
  ASSISTANT CITY CLERK
